title: Differentials of A[x]/(x^p - a) in characteristic p
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, $A$ a commutative ring with $p\cdot1_A=0$ (an $\mathbf F_p$-algebra), $a_1,\dots,a_n\in A$, and $A'=A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^p-a_1,\dots,x_n^p-a_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $\Omega$, $\mathrm d$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then: (1) $\Omega_{A'/A}$ is a free $A'$-module with basis $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$ (images of the variables); (2) the sequence of $A'$-modules $$A'^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\ }A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{\ w\ }\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{\ z\ }\Omega_{A'/A}\to0,$$ with $\varepsilon(e_j)=1\otimes\mathrm da_j$, $w(c\otimes\mathrm da)=c\,\mathrm d(a\cdot1_{A'})$ and $z(c\,\mathrm dc')=c\,\mathrm dc'$, is exact.

The Jacobi-Zariski sequence for F_p -> A -> A' ... the jth basis vector of H_1(L_{A'/A}) maps to da_j (x) 1'; tags 00S4 (algebra-lemma-change-base-NL) and 00S2 verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: For P=A[X_j] and I=(X_j^p-C(a_j)), the ZMod p-algebra structure gives p=0 in P. Leibniz and differentiation of constants give d(X_j^p-C(a_j))=0 over A. Submodule.span_induction then proves 1 tensor dg=0 for every g in I: in the scalar case d(rg)=r dg+g dr, and g acts by zero on B=P/I. This is the proved helper relative_relation_zero.

proof.text: The conormal map kerCotangentToTensor A P B is zero: lift each conormal class to a kernel representative and use the preceding computation. exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange then makes mapBaseChange A P B injective, while mapBaseChange_surjective makes it surjective. Base-change mvPolynomialBasis A (Fin n) to B and transport along LinearEquiv.ofBijective. Basis.map_apply, Basis.baseChange_apply and map_D identify its vectors with the differentials of the quotient variables. This proves relative_basis.

proof.text: Construct the chosen generators Q for the quotient using the actual surjective quotient map and its section. Polynomial extensionality identifies aeval Q.val with the quotient algebra map, hence Q.ker=I. Every conormal class is a cycle by the first step. Use the presentation connecting map and coefficient map c from [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-connecting-map-exact]. The monomial and constant formulas compute c(X_j^p-C(a_j))=-1 tensor d(a_j). No assertion that H1 is free or comparison with the canonical presentation is needed.

proof.text: Let epsilon be the stated linear combination map. Ideal-span induction shows c(g) belongs to range epsilon for all g in I. For the generators this is the negative of epsilon(single j 1); addition follows by linearity. For rg use c(rg)=r c(g)+g c(r), where the second term vanishes in B and the first belongs to the B-submodule range epsilon. Every H1 class lifts to a conormal representative g, so its connecting image belongs to range epsilon. Conversely epsilon(single j 1) is the connecting image of the negative relation cycle. Finsupp.range_linearCombination and span_le therefore give equality of the two ranges. Exactness from [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-connecting-map-exact] now gives the first exactness assertion.

split_report.summary: Split into 6 steps following More on Algebra 07E5 (2)=>(4) (lines 8785-8825), using only existing nodes, no new node. Step 1: d(x_j^p - a_j) = p x_j^{p-1} dx_j = 0 in Omega_{P/A} (polynomial Kaehler basis leaf), so 1 (x) dg = 0 for g in I. Step 2: clause (1) from the 00RU leaf (jacobi-zariski-differential-maps) with delta = 0 and the base-changed basis of the any-variables Kaehler leaf. Step 3: H_1 of the presentation alpha is I/I^2, generated by the f_j. Step 4: comparison of alpha with the canonical presentation by the 00S1 leaf (nl-presentation-h1-functoriality): phi: x_i -> [x_i] and a section chi give inverse maps on H_1, so H_1(L_{A'/A}) is generated by the classes of [x_j]^p - a_j. Step 5: the Jacobi-Zariski sequence of F_p -> A -> A' (00S2 node, reviewed) with its explicit connecting map gives partial(h_j) = -1 (x) da_j. Step 6: im partial = im epsilon, giving (2). The source's freeness of H_1(L_{A'/A}) (via 00S4, which needs flatness over the field k) is neither stated by the item nor needed (only generation by the f_j is used), so no regular-sequence/Koszul node is needed. Sign: the connecting map sends h_j to -da_j (x) 1, not da_j (x) 1 as the source writes; images agree. The citer lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-h1-injective uses exactly (1) and (2) as stated. Mathlib re-searched (leansearch, loogle, leanfinder, grep, local_search): no match.
